review_scope: Independent masked review using only frozen/judge-operator.txt and reviews/final-masked-packet.json. All findings below apply to the exact UTF-8 texts identified by the verified hashes, including their final newlines.

A.word_count_method: Whitespace-delimited; hyphenated expressions count as one word.

B.word_count_method: Whitespace-delimited; hyphenated expressions count as one word.

A.finding: Recommends a six-week extension to test access and booking reliability before deciding whether to add rooms.

B.finding: Recommends the same six-week access and reliability test before considering more rooms; later specifies the expansion decision conditions.

A.finding: Identifies the first eight weeks and explicitly treats reservations as evidence of demand without establishing reliable access.

B.finding: States the same bounded conclusion for the first eight weeks, followed by the supporting reservation counts.

A.finding: Preserves two rooms, free two-hour bookings, and staffed opening hours.

B.finding: Preserves two rooms, free two-hour bookings, and staffed hours.

A.finding: Preserves 160 available slots, 118 reserved, and 91 used; the later 27 unused reservations makes the reservation/use relationship consistent.

B.finding: Preserves 118 reserved out of 160 slots and 91 used; the later 27 unused reservations preserves the same accounting.

A.finding: Preserves 42 voluntary respondents, 25 valuing predictable study or small-group space, and 17 reporting finding/completion difficulties.

B.finding: Preserves all three counts, the voluntary respondent denominator, both uses of the space, and both types of booking difficulty.

A.finding: Explicitly says voluntary responses cannot establish how common difficulties are among residents.

B.finding: Voluntary responses cannot establish how widespread difficulties are. The resident population is implicit in the article context; there is no prevalence claim.

A.finding: Preserves four repeat bookers accounting for 18 of 27 unused reservations and most never-reserved slots occurring before noon on weekdays.

B.finding: Preserves the same actors, 18/27 relationship, weekday-morning timing, and distinction between unused reservations and slots never reserved.

A.finding: Presents cancellation habits and residents' availability as possibilities, labels the availability explanation untested, and says unused reservations alone do not establish the extent of unmet demand.

B.finding: Presents both explanations as possible and unestablished; unused reservations alone do not measure unmet demand. No cause is treated as observed.

A.finding: Explicitly limits the ability of additional rooms to resolve cancellation habits or the timing/availability mismatch.

B.finding: Says adding rooms would not necessarily address either problem, referring clearly to the two immediately preceding possible explanations.

A.finding: The opening states the practical access test; existing access constraints and proposed remedies explain its purpose.

B.finding: The opening and access paragraph preserve the need to test access before expansion, without requiring the original transitional sentence.

A.finding: Preserves mandatory email for the online form and dependence on the front-desk supervisor for telephone bookings.

B.finding: Preserves both access constraints and identifies the same responsible role.

A.finding: Correctly identifies three of the 17 difficulty respondents as reporting that one of the two barriers prevented booking; preserves reported rather than independently verified experience.

B.finding: Correctly identifies three of the 17 and names the email requirement or limited telephone coverage as the reported barrier.

A.finding: Proposes that any trained desk worker take telephone and in-person reservations during the extension, sharing inventory with online bookings.

B.finding: Preserves any trained desk worker, both additional booking routes, the extension timing, and one inventory for every route.

A.finding: Proposes reminders and a simple cancellation option, describes releasing unwanted reservations as a possible benefit, and explicitly says effectiveness is unmeasured.

B.finding: Reminders and simple cancellation express the same proposed facility and possible release benefit; effectiveness remains explicitly unmeasured.

A.finding: Assigns training and publication to the service manager; preserves weekly reservation, attendance, cancellation, and unfulfilled-request totals by route and time of day.

B.finding: Preserves the manager's responsibilities, weekly frequency, all four measures, and both breakdowns; unaccommodated requests accurately names requests that could not be accommodated.

A.finding: Assigns consistent request recording to desk workers, including when rooms are full.

B.finding: Preserves the same responsibility and includes requests received when rooms are full.

A.finding: Places consideration of expansion after six weeks, clearly referring to the proposed extension established at the start.

B.finding: Explicitly places the expansion decision after the six-week extension.

A.finding: Makes all three proposed conditions necessary: trained staff for every staffed opening period; at least 85% of extension reservations used or cancelled before start; unfulfilled requests recorded in at least four of six weeks despite changes.

B.finding: Preserves all three necessary proposed conditions, the extension-reservation denominator, timely cancellation, and four-of-six-week persistence despite changes. The preceding recording duties make these recorded requests. The added cancellation/use distinction correctly interprets the threshold.

A.finding: Meeting the conditions supports considering expansion and does not establish the number of additional rooms; no approval or sufficiency guarantee is introduced.

B.finding: Retains support for considering expansion and the inability to establish room quantity; does not turn the criteria into an automatic expansion decision.

A.finding: If staff coverage or booking reliability remains weak, requires revising the booking process and reassessing before expansion.

B.finding: Preserves revision and reassessment before expansion if coverage or reliability remains weak; both refer clearly to the preceding staffing and reservation conditions.

A.finding: All substantive facts and qualifications in F01-F24 are retained. The fictional institution is named without inserting provenance or experiment labels into the intended article. No actors, observed effects, measurements, or causal findings are invented.

B.finding: All substantive facts and qualifications in F01-F24 are retained, including through clear paragraph context. The additional sentence about timely cancellation is a logical clarification of F21: a reservation can count through cancellation without establishing subsequent use. It asserts no new observation or measured effect. No provenance or experiment labels appear in the article.

concrete_findings: Leads with the recommendation and its purpose, then moves from counts and limitations to the access changes, responsibilities, and decision conditions.
Directly links reservations to evidence of demand and explicitly identifies residents as the population whose difficulty prevalence remains unknown.
The final paragraph is information-dense, but its semicolons make the three necessary conditions distinguishable.
Uses the same coherent decision sequence and keeps the counts, access changes, and assigned responsibilities understandable.
Explicitly says neither causal explanation is established and anchors the final decision to the six-week extension.

The extra cancellation sentence helps distinguish the reliability threshold from actual room use, while adding some weight to an already dense final paragraph. The compound unaccommodated-request is slightly cumbersome but understandable.

quality_assessment.length_and_audience: Both meet the approximately 300-350-word request and use an appropriate explanatory, professional tone for staff and residents. Neither requires technical background.

preference_reasons: Both texts pass all 20 claims, preserve the protected literals, and support the same informed decision without source omissions or invented factual claims.
A is somewhat more explicit about the resident population and the link between reservations and demand; B adds a useful explanation of what timely cancellation does and does not establish.
These are small, balanced clarity differences. Neither text has a material advantage in completeness, readability, relevance, or tone that warrants selecting a winner.
